title: Medical and attendance supporting-evidence handling - observed 2023-2024 packet
summary: One restricted employee packet shows how attendance evidence was historically assembled around a standardized Attendance Calendar: dated message screenshots, provider-document images and contextual evidence were retained together. The evidence demonstrates an intake/archive pattern, not a current approved communication channel.

claims.claim: The restricted packet contains a two-page 2023/2024 Attendance Calendar plus 18 date-named image artifacts retained as supporting evidence.

evidence.note: Employee identity and medical details excluded.

claims.claim: Visual classification of the 18 image artifacts identifies 13 messaging-app conversation screenshots, four standalone photos/screenshots of provider or medical-document pages, and one contextual weather/road-condition image; several message screenshots also contain attached document images.

evidence.page_or_section: 18 restricted images - visual document-type classification only
evidence.note: No message text, diagnosis, provider name or medical content is promoted.

claims.claim: The supporting artifacts are date-named and span multiple attendance events, indicating that date-based provenance was used to associate informal communications and documentation with the attendance record.

The packet shows that historical attendance evidence could arrive through informal digital communication as well as formal provider documentation; those evidence types should be distinguished rather than treated as equivalent.

evidence.note: This does not establish messaging as the current approved submission channel.

claims.claim: The current 2025 handbook authorizes supervisors to request a doctor's excuse and requires documentation for certain absences/FMLA, but it does not establish text messaging or photographed notes as the authoritative submission method.

A separate 2013 intermittent-FMLA record instructed employees to send supporting documentation directly to Human Resources rather than attaching it to timesheets or ordinary absence requests, providing historical support for separating sensitive supporting documents from ordinary time/attendance records.

evidence.page_or_section: restricted 2013 intermittent-FMLA counseling record - generalized routing instruction

trigger: Employee absence/tardy event is supported by medical, provider, communication or contextual evidence.
prerequisites: Identify the attendance event and applicable policy category.
Use restricted access for medical/supporting documents.
systems: Messaging or other intake channel where permitted
steps: Capture the source channel and received date for each supporting artifact.
Classify the artifact as employee communication, provider document, contextual evidence or other evidence.
Link the artifact to the applicable attendance/leave event using a stable event ID.
Store sensitive medical/provider documents in the restricted medical/leave repository, not the ordinary attendance ledger.
Record only the minimum attendance-relevant metadata in the general attendance view.
Retain original evidence/provenance rather than relying on a copied filename or summary.
decisions: Whether evidence is sufficient under current policy.
Whether the event is protected/FMLA/workers' compensation or ordinary attendance.
Whether an informal communication must be followed by an original/formal document.
exceptions: Emergency notification may arrive informally, but informal channel use does not establish final documentation sufficiency.
controls: Medical/provider content must remain restricted and logically separate from ordinary personnel/timekeeping views.
Do not infer diagnoses or global rules from an employee's communications.
Preserve received date, source channel and original artifact hash.
Distinguish employee statements from independent provider documentation and contextual evidence.
Do not assume text-message screenshots are the current authoritative intake channel.
unresolved_questions: What is the current approved intake channel for doctor's notes, medical releases and FMLA supporting documents?
Are original paper/provider documents required after a photo or message attachment is received?
Where are medical/leave records currently stored, and how is access separated from the general personnel file?
What retention rules apply to attendance-supporting message screenshots and contextual evidence?
automation_candidates: Restricted evidence inbox that classifies communication/provider/context artifacts and links them to attendance events without exposing medical content in the attendance ledger.
Hash and timestamp every supporting artifact and retain its original source-channel metadata.
Generate follow-up tasks when an informal message/photo needs a formal provider document or original copy.
Scanner rule that routes medical/provider notes to restricted storage while emitting only attendance-relevant metadata to the normal HR record.

provenance.notes: Only artifact types, dates/provenance structure and form structure were generalized; all employee/medical content remains restricted.
